events.text: USS Slater laid down at Tampa Shipbuilding Company, Florida.

evidence.quote: USS Slater was laid down on 9 March 1943

events.label: convoy escort
events.text: Escorted two convoys to the United Kingdom in the latter part of 1944.

evidence.quote: In the latter part of 1944 , Slater escorted two convoys to the United Kingdom

events.label: christening
events.text: Ship christened by Lenora Slater, mother of the namesake.

evidence.quote: she was christened on 20 Feb 1944 by Lenora Slater

events.text: USS Slater launched.

evidence.quote: launched on 20 February 1944

events.text: USS Slater commissioned into the United States Navy.

evidence.quote: The ship was commissioned on 1 May 1944

events.label: shakedown cruise
events.text: Shakedown cruise near Bermuda.

evidence.quote: After a shakedown cruise near Bermuda in June 1944

events.label: convoy escort
events.text: Continued convoy escort service begins.

evidence.quote: She continued serving in this capacity from January 1945 until May 1945

events.label: convoy escort
events.text: Convoy escort service ends.

evidence.quote: She continued serving in this capacity from January 1945 until May 1945

events.text: Passed through the Panama Canal on the way to the Pacific.

evidence.quote: She went through the Panama Canal on 28 June 1945

events.text: Joined Task Unit 33.2.4 at Manila and escorted it to Yokohama.

evidence.quote: From there she joined Task Unit 33.2.4 at Manila in September

events.label: deactivation
events.text: Placed in the reserve fleet at Green Cove Springs, Florida.

evidence.quote: Slater was placed in the reserve fleet at Green Cove Springs ,
Florida in 1947

events.text: Transferred to the Hellenic Navy under the Truman Doctrine.

evidence.quote: On 1 March 1951 , Slater was transferred to the Hellenic Navy under the Truman Doctrine
the ship was transferred to Greece and renamed Aetos

events.text: Renamed Aetos (Eagle) with pennant D01 in Greek service.

evidence.quote: On 1 March 1951 , Slater was transferred to the Hellenic Navy under the Truman Doctrine , and renamed Aetos

events.label: filming
events.text: Ship appeared in Greek film Alice in the Navy while in Greek service.

evidence.quote: Alice in the Navy , filmed in 1961

events.text: Decommissioned from the Hellenic Navy as Aetos.

evidence.quote: Aetos was decommissioned in 1991
Decommissioned in 1991

events.text: Greece donated the ship to the Destroyer Escort Sailors Association.

evidence.quote: Aetos was decommissioned in 1991 , and Greece donated the ship to the Destroyer Escort Sailors Association

events.text: Towed by a Russian tugboat from Crete to New York City.

evidence.quote: A Russian ocean-going tugboat towed the ship from Crete to New York City in 1993

events.text: Arrived at the Port of Albany, New York, as a museum ship.

evidence.quote: On Sunday 26 October 1997 , Slater arrived at the Port of Albany

events.label: heritage listing
events.text: Listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

evidence.quote: On 7 May 1998 , Slater was listed on the National Register of Historic Places

events.label: fire
events.text: Welder accidentally started a fire aboard, causing minor damage.

evidence.quote: In January 2006 , a welder accidentally started a fire
aboard Slater which caused some minor damage to the ship

events.label: filming
events.text: Part of Japanese film Orion in Midsummer filmed on board.

evidence.quote: In August 2008 part of the Japanese film Orion in Midsummer was filmed on board

events.label: collision
events.text: Struck by the Hudson River touring ship Dutch Apple.

evidence.quote: USS Slater was struck by the Hudson River touring ship Dutch Apple on 10 September 2019

undated_mentions: Sent to Key West to serve as target ship and sonar school ship (after June 1944)
Headed to the Pacific after the war in Europe ended
Stopped at San Diego before sailing to Pearl Harbor (1945)
Second Panama Canal passage en route to Norfolk for deactivation
Destroyer escort sailors donated more than a quarter of a million dollars to bring Slater to the United States
Albany, New York chosen as permanent home for the ship
Repairs completed within a few months after the 2006 fire
Refits: depth-charge racks and K-guns removed, twin Bofors 40 mm guns added, single 20 mm guns replaced with twin mounts
